findings.observation: Sheet 5, Block 7 contains a section titled 'AUSTIN ENERGY STANDARD NOTES' with 5 numbered notes. I reviewed notes 1-4 against the expected template notes from the General Site Plan Notes reference document. Note 1 covers tree pruning/easement rights and Chapter 25-8 compliance. Note 2 covers easement/access requirements for electric facilities. Note 3 covers owner responsibility for erosion control and tree work within 10 feet of overhead electrical facilities. Note 4 covers clearance maintenance per NESC, OSHA, and related regulations. All 4 required notes are present. Note 5 addresses relocation costs and is an additional note not required by the template.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 4 standard Austin Energy notes covering: (1) tree pruning/easement rights, (2) easement/access obligations, (3) erosion control responsibilities, and (4) NESC/OSHA clearance maintenance. The validation methodology specifies approximately 90% semantic matching - notes do not need to be character-for-character identical but must preserve substantive meaning and regulatory references. Comparing the plan notes to the template: Note 1 matches the tree pruning language and Chapter 25-8 Subchapter B citation exactly (aside from capitalization). Note 2 matches the easement/access language and Chapter 25-8 citation exactly. Note 3 matches the erosion control and tree work language, including the 10-foot centerline reference. Note 4 matches the NESC/OSHA clearance language. All substantive requirements and regulatory citations are preserved. The notes appear on a General Notes Sheet as permitted by the flexible location binding. This meets the ~90% semantic threshold.
findings.explanation: All 4 required Austin Energy standard notes found on Sheet 5, Block 7, with substantive content matching template requirements.

findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Existing Conditions & Demolition Plan) includes a legend in Block 5 with symbols for existing overhead electric (OHU), existing electric manhole (E), existing electric meter (E), existing power pole, and existing guy anchor. Block 2 description mentions 'existing electric manholes' as specific features on the site plan. Sheet 18 (Overall Utility Plan) Block 1 description lists 'underground electric' and callouts include 'ELECTRIC MANHOLE' for existing facilities. The legend on Sheet 18 Block 3 includes a symbol for 'EXISTING ELECTRIC MANHOLE'.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires existing electric utility facilities (overhead and underground) to be shown on plan sheets. The location binding is 'explicit' for 'all plan sheets', meaning the facilities must be depicted somewhere in the plan set. Sheet 8 provides comprehensive existing conditions symbology for both overhead electric lines (OHU designation) and underground facilities (electric manholes, meters, power poles, guy anchors). Sheet 18 reinforces this by showing existing electric manholes on the overall utility plan. Together, these sheets document the existing electric infrastructure baseline required for downstream reviewers to verify conflicts and clearances. Both overhead and underground existing facilities are accounted for across the plan set.
findings.explanation: Existing electric facilities (overhead and underground) shown on Sheets 8 and 18, including electric manholes, meters, power poles, and overhead lines.

findings.observation: Sheet 18 (Overall Utility Plan) Block 1 description lists 'underground electric' as a feature on the plan. Callouts in Block 1 include 'UNDERGROUND ELECTRIC LINE (SEE PLANS BY OTHERS)', '48" ELECTRIC PULL BOX' (appearing multiple times), 'ELECTRIC MANHOLE', and 'VARIABLE WIDTH ELECTRIC CLEARANCE'. Sheet 18 Block 3 legend includes symbols and labels for: proposed electric easement (---E---), proposed underground electric line (---UGE---), proposed pull box (square with E), proposed electric manhole (circle with E), proposed transformer (square with T), and proposed switchgear (square with S).
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires proposed electric utility facilities to be shown on plan sheets. The location binding is 'explicit' for 'all plan sheets', meaning the facilities must be depicted somewhere in the plan set. Sheet 18 provides a comprehensive depiction of proposed underground electric infrastructure, including underground electric lines, pull boxes, manholes, transformers, and switchgear. The legend clearly differentiates proposed facilities from existing ones. The callout 'SEE PLANS BY OTHERS' indicates coordination with separate electrical plans prepared by the MEP engineer, which is standard practice - the site plan shows routing and locations while detailed electrical design is on MEP sheets. The presence of proposed electric easements, clearances, and specific equipment locations (pull boxes, manholes) demonstrates sufficient detail for Austin Energy to verify service routing and conflicts at the completeness stage. Proposed facilities are shown.
findings.explanation: Proposed electric facilities shown on Sheet 18, including underground electric lines, pull boxes, manholes, transformers, and switchgear with coordination note to MEP plans.

findings.observation: Sheet 1, Block 10 (Legal Description block) states 'ZONING = CS-V-CO & CS-V-DBSO'. This indicates the site is zoned Commercial Services (CS) with Vertical Mixed Use combining district (-V), Conditional Overlay (-CO), and Density Bonus 90 overlay (-DBSO, referring to DB90). Facts.md confirms the three tracts have zoning designations CS-V-DB90, CS-V-CO, and CS-V-CO. None of the parcels are zoned CBD (Central Business District) or DMU (Downtown Mixed Use).
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a Letter of Intent signed by Green Building Program staff and development point of contact, but the condition is 'If zoned CBD or DMU'. The site zoning is CS-V with overlays (CO and DB90). CS-V is Commercial Services with Vertical Mixed Use, which is distinct from the downtown base zoning districts CBD and DMU. The grouping overview explains that the AEGB LOI requirement at site plan stage applies specifically to CBD/DMU sites under Downtown Design provisions. Since this site is not in a downtown zoning district, the trigger condition for AEGB-02 is not met. The item is not applicable to this site plan.
findings.explanation: Site is zoned CS-V-CO & CS-V-DBSO, not CBD or DMU, so AEGB Letter of Intent requirement does not apply.

summary: 3 of 4 items pass, 0 fail, 1 not-applicable. All required Austin Energy standard notes are present and electric facilities are properly depicted.
